<reason>B establishes a stronger comparative case for enforceable advance disclosure alongside liability. A raises legitimate concerns about comparability, sensitive findings, and compliance costs, but repeatedly equates imperfect information with no information and the absence of a deployment veto with no prevention. B directly answers both pressure questions and explains protected redactions, public scrutiny, and preventive incentives. A concedes its alternative cannot compel pre-launch disclosure and never sufficiently establishes that the mandate’s costs outweigh that benefit.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B defeats A’s attempted contradiction about reputation by distinguishing punishment after harm from pressure generated by mandatory disclosure before deployment. B also correctly rejects A’s unsupported claim that publishing findings turns compliance into a liability waiver.</best_rebuttal>
